Method of Attack: Uses virtualization software to deploy a Linux XMRig coinminer variant on Windows and macOS systems via a Tiny Core Linux virtual machine
Bundled within cracked copies of Windows and macOS VST software
Persistence via plist files on macOS and batch scripts on Windows
Uses QEMU for macOS and VirtualBox for Windows to run the Linux coinminer VM
Updates performed via scripts communicating with command-and-control server via SCP
CPU monitor script on macOS to start/stop mining based on CPU usage and Activity Monitor process
Discoverer: ESET Research's detection engineer Michal Malik
Attack Vector: Installation of pirated VST host software bundled with virtualization software and Linux image
Attacker-controlled website distributing cracked VST software
Indicators of Compromise: 137 VST-related apps linked from attacker-controlled website
plist files in /Library/LaunchDaemons with RunAtLoad and KeepAlive set to true on macOS
Batch scripts launching coinminer Linux image as a service on Windows
Communication with LoudMiner's command-and-control (C2) server via SCP
